origin: The headline and first sentence state as fact a US yen purchase that rests on one newspaper's anonymous sources, with no comment from the Treasury, the New York Fed or the banks. The fact sheet makes US action plausible (banks put on alert, Bessent's notepad) but shows no confirmation, a Treasury secretary who had publicly dismissed intervention talk six months earlier, and a 2011 precedent in which the US bought dollars against the yen rather than yen. The trade mechanics (euros, the New York Fed, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley) are uncheckable on the fact sheet. Expected honest rating: 55 to 75.
